chief_complaint: intense, unbearable eye itching, watery tearing, and stringy white discharge with cobblestone eyelid bumps during spring pollen season
hpi_details: 22F presenting with bilateral severe ocular pruritus, conjunctival chemosis, and giant papillae on tarsal conjunctiva responding rapidly to topical antihistamine/mast cell stabilizer drops (Olopatadine or Ketotifen).
ideas: She thinks her eyes are having an extreme reaction to the spring tree pollen bloom outside.
concerns: She is worried that the unbearable itching and swelling will prevent her from studying for her upcoming college final exams.
expectations: She hopes to receive prescription-strength allergy eye drops because over-the-counter drops have not provided any relief.

Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.

Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Allergic Conjunctivitis Seasonal Eruption.

reference_soap.plan: Recommend allergen avoidance, cool compresses, and topical antihistamine/mast-cell-stabilizer drops such as olopatadine or ketotifen as appropriate. Avoid rubbing the eyes. Arrange ophthalmology assessment for pain, photophobia, reduced vision, corneal involvement, or symptoms not responding to treatment.

teaching.one_liner: 22F with intense bilateral itching, watery tearing, and stringy discharge during spring pollen season.
red_flags: Itching as the dominant symptom favors allergy over infection

must_ask.objective: Confirm itching as the dominant symptom
must_ask.say: Is itching the main problem, more than pain or discharge?

must_ask.objective: Ask about seasonal or allergen triggers
must_ask.say: Does this happen every spring, or around specific things like pets or dust?
Do you also have a runny nose or sneezing along with this?
Is the discharge stringy or watery, rather than thick and yellow?

history.answer: My eyes have been intensely itchy and watering constantly for the past two days.
It started two days ago in both eyes at the same time and has been getting steadily more bothersome.
The entire white part of both of my eyes looks pink and swollen, but there is no distinct bloody red spot.
I don't have deep eye pain, just an intense gritty burning feeling whenever I can't resist rubbing them.
My eyesight is completely normal, though it gets momentarily blurry when tears well up in my eyes.
No, normal indoor lighting and sunlight do not cause any pain in my eyes.
No, I haven't seen any colored halos around lights, and I don't have any headache or nausea.
It is mostly clear watery tears mixed with stringy white mucus, and my eyelids are not glued shut when I wake up.
The itching is unbearable and constant; it is definitely the worst part of this entire problem.
Both of my eyelids are puffy, and when I flip the upper lid it feels like there are rough cobblestone bumps underneath, but there are no painful styes.
No, moving my eyes doesn't hurt, my eyes aren't bulging, I don't see double, and I haven't had a fever.
I haven't had a cold, fever, or sore throat recently, and nobody at home or school has had pink eye.
I do not wear contact lenses; I only wear prescription glasses sometimes while studying.
No, I haven't had any eye injury, nothing scratched my eyes, and no chemicals splashed into them.
Yes, this flare-up happens every spring when pollen counts surge, and I also get sneezing fits and a runny nose.
I don't usually suffer from dry eyes or dry mouth, but breezy outdoor air definitely makes the itchiness flare up.
No, I don't have morning back stiffness, swollen joints, painful mouth ulcers, or diarrhea.
No, I have never had cold sores or shingles, and there are no blisters on my forehead or nose.
No, I don't take blood thinners, my blood pressure is normal, and I haven't been coughing hard or straining.
I have never had eye surgery, eye trauma, or glaucoma, just these recurring spring allergy episodes.

My college finals start next week, and I'm terrified I won't be able to read my computer screen or study with my eyes itching like this. I'm hoping you can prescribe some strong allergy drops that actually work, because the drugstore artificial tears haven't done anything.
I have seasonal allergic rhinitis, but no other chronic illnesses like diabetes or high blood pressure.
I have never undergone any surgical procedures and have never been admitted to a hospital.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 118/74 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.6 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
Alert young female in no acute distress, with mildly swollen eyelids and occasional dabbing at watery eyes with a tissue.

Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes; pupils are equal, round, and briskly reactive to light; extraocular movements are full without pain or diplopia; cornea is clear without epithelial defect or fluorescein uptake.

Diffuse conjunctival injection and marked chemosis in both eyes with stringy white mucoid discharge; upper eyelid eversion reveals giant cobblestone papillae on the tarsal conjunctiva without foreign bodies.
Nasal mucosa is pale and boggy with clear watery secretions; posterior oropharynx is normal without erythema or tonsillar exudate.
No preauricular, submandibular, or anterior cervical lymphadenopathy palpable.
No tenderness over the frontal or maxillary sinuses, and no erythema or tenderness over the lacrimal sac region.
No vesicles, rashes, or eczema noted on the face, forehead, or periocular skin.
